key_insight: Language models can act as Research World Models that predict experimental outcomes, and their predictions improve when they are trained with real research experience from the same or related environments.
engineering_relevance: For AI research agents, outcome prediction can reduce wasted experiments and improve selection under tight compute budgets, making self-improving research systems more practical.
method: Built RWMs to rank/predict the outcomes of candidate research interventions across pretraining, post-training, and inference environments.
Evaluated transfer from in-environment and cross-environment research experience, including multi-round Autoresearch under fixed selection budgets.
Compared 13 language models and tested whether adding research knowledge helps more than scaling model choice or reasoning effort.
evidence_signal: The study analyzes over 2,600 experimental records from nine environments and more than 171,000 H100 GPU-hours, reporting gains such as +0.27 Spearman and 78% lower selection regret in a cross-environment setting.
watch_item: Performance depends on accumulated experimental data, so RWMs may be weaker in truly novel environments with little or no prior research history.
paper_title: Language Models as AI Research World Models
